questions.q: In adults, the paranasal sinus most commonly involved in sinusitis is the:
questions.why: The maxillary sinus is most often affected in adults; the ethmoids are most often affected in children.

questions.q: According to Hahnemann, the physician should also be a preserver of health by knowing and removing:
opts: the exciting and maintaining causes of disease
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §4 and the note to §7.

questions.q: The name of the software RADAR stands for:
opts: Rapid Aid to Drug Aimed Research
Rapid Analysis of Disease And Remedy
questions.why: RADAR, from Archibel in Belgium, is short for Rapid Aid to Drug Aimed Research.

questions.q: A dry, spasmodic cough at night that is worse on lying down and relieved by sitting up, in a jealous, suspicious patient, suggests:
questions.why: Hyoscyamus: dry nocturnal cough worse lying down, better sitting up (Boericke).

questions.q: Irregular, spasmodic false labour pains that fly about the abdomen, with a rigid os and great exhaustion, call for:
questions.why: Caulophyllum is the classic remedy for spasmodic, ineffectual pains with rigidity of the os and weakness.

questions.q: Pin-point pupils, excessive salivation and sweating, muscle fasciculations and a kerosene-like smell suggest poisoning by:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Cholinergic crisis; serum cholinesterase is low. Datura dilates the pupils.

questions.q: The most specific serum marker of myocardial injury is:
questions.why: Troponins are specific to heart muscle and stay raised for days; CK-MB, AST and LDH are less specific.

questions.q: The birth dose of hepatitis B vaccine under the UIP should be given:
opts: any time in the first year
questions.why: Hep B birth dose is effective in preventing perinatal transmission only if given within 24 hours.

questions.q: Which remedy is complementary to Pulsatilla?
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla; Kali sulph is also complementary.

questions.q: Regarding a dying declaration recorded by a doctor, which statement is correct?
opts: The accused must be present and may cross-examine
It is valid only if recorded by a magistrate
It must be made in the presence of a police officer
No oath is given, and the doctor should certify that the declarant was conscious and of sound mind
questions.why: A dying declaration needs no oath and no presence of the accused; the doctor certifies compos mentis. The dying deposition, with the accused present, is recorded by a magistrate.
